situation: My coworker Jen presented our joint churn analysis to the VP yesterday and kept saying 'I found' for work I did. We're peers. I want to raise it with her one on one.
reply: Hey Jen, can I give you some feedback on yesterday's VP review? When you walked through the churn analysis, the parts I did came out as 'I found', so the VP had no way of knowing they were mine. I don't think you meant it that way. What's your read? For the next one, could we split the slides so each of us presents our own part?
note: Observation, impact, then pause for her side before the ask; there may be context you don't have.

situation: Just had a feedback conversation with my report Kevin about typos in client emails. We agreed he'll read client emails aloud before sending, and for the next month send anything to a new client to me first. Need the short written follow-up.
reply: Thanks for the chat this afternoon, Kevin. To capture it: client emails get a read-aloud check before sending, and for the next month anything to a new client comes to me for a quick look first. Let's check in on 13 November. Tell me if I've missed anything.
note: Neutral and short. The follow-up records the agreement, not the criticism.

situation: On 8 September I told my direct report Aisha she needs to be at our 9:30 standup on time. She's been late four times since, including today. I want to say it firmly in our 1:1.
reply: On 8 September we agreed you'd be at standup by 9:30, and you've been late four times since, including today. I need this to change now, and I'll be tracking it in our one-to-ones. What's getting in the way?
note: Name the agreement and the facts, make the consequence clear, and put it in writing after. If it continues, go to HR rather than repeating the conversation.

situation: 我是小组长，上周私下跟组员小周说过，他的周报数据连着两次算错，让他发之前自己核一遍。今天这份又错了，我提了一句，他回我：大家周报都有错，你怎么只盯着我。
reply: 我明白你觉得被单独挑出来了。其他人的周报有问题，我也会单独找他们谈，这里不拿你跟别人比。我们说的是你这边：最近三份周报都有数据算错。要求还是一样，另外加一步：接下来两周，周报周五下午四点前先发我过一遍再发出去。10月16号周五我们再聊聊效果。
note: 只有情绪、没有新信息的反驳：平静重复要求，给一个具体的支持措施和复盘日期，不展开辩论。

situation: My manager Greg keeps sending me 'urgent for Monday' tasks on Slack after 6pm on Fridays. Third week running, I worked Sunday again. I want to raise it in our 1:1 this Thursday without sounding like I'm complaining.
reply: Can I give you some feedback on how Friday requests reach me? The last three Fridays, urgent tasks have come in on Slack after 6pm for Monday morning, and I've ended up working Sundays to hit them. What's driving the timing on your side? If those could reach me by 3pm on Friday, or carry a Tuesday deadline when they land later, I can plan around them properly and still turn them round fast.
note: Upward feedback uses the same shape: ask first, the facts with a count, the impact, a real question, then an ask that makes his job easier too.

situation: 我是设计组长。同级的产品经理老吴上周四在需求评审会上当着大家说我组里刚来两个月的设计师小林的方案“完全没想过用户”，小林会后哭了。老吴人不坏，就是说话冲，我想私下跟他聊聊。
reply: 老吴，有空聊五分钟吗？想说说上周四评审会的事。你说小林的方案“完全没想过用户”，我知道你是着急方案有问题，但她刚来两个月，当着全组听到这句，会后挺难受的。你当时主要觉得哪块有问题？以后评审遇到这种情况，能不能直接说具体是哪个环节，或者会后单独跟我说，我带她改。下周评审完我们再碰一下，看看效果。
note: 对平级同事：先征得同意，说具体一句话和它对团队的影响，先问他的看法，再提具体做法，并约好回头看。

situation: I manage a dev team. Marcus, a senior engineer, left three comments on junior dev Leah's pull request last Thursday that just said 'wrong, redo'. She told me she's now nervous about opening PRs. I'm raising it in our 1:1 tomorrow.
reply: Can I give you some feedback on code reviews? On Leah's pull request last Thursday, three of your comments said 'wrong, redo' with no explanation. She's told me she's now nervous about opening PRs at all. What's your read on it? Going forward, I'd like every blocking comment to say what's wrong and point to one direction for the fix. Let's look at a couple of your reviews together on Tuesday 13 October.
note: A 1:1 script: pause after 'What's your read on it?' and actually listen before giving the ask; keep Leah's name out of it if he'd take it out on her.

situation: Yesterday I told my report Hannah that her weekly client reports keep arriving Monday afternoon instead of by 9am. She explained her kid's school start moved and she can't be online before 10 now. I didn't know. I want to follow up in writing with a revised ask.
reply: Thanks for telling me about the school run yesterday, that's useful context and I'm glad I know. What still matters is that clients have their reports when their week starts. So here's the adjusted ask: finish them by Friday 5pm and schedule them to send at 9am Monday, starting this week. If a Friday gets tight, tell me by Thursday and we'll move something off your plate. Let's check how it's going on Friday 16 October.
note: When pushback brings real context, change the ask, not the goal, and still put a check-in date on it.

situation: I manage an account manager, Dev. Twice this month he's promised clients a delivery date on the call without checking with production, and last Friday we had to walk back the Kessler date, which made us look bad. We have our 1:1 tomorrow.
reply: Can I give you some feedback on client commitments? On the Kessler call you confirmed a delivery date before checking with production, and last Friday we had to walk it back. That's the second time this month, and it makes our dates look unreliable to clients. What's your read on how it happened? Going forward, when a client asks for a date, tell them you'll confirm within 24 hours, and check with production first. Let's look at your next two commitments together on Tuesday 13 October.
note: One behaviour, one dated example with its real cost, a genuine question, then a line he can use on the very next call.

situation: Ich bin Teamlead in einem Remote-Team. Jonas aus dem Plattform-Team (gleiche Ebene) beantwortet Slack-Fragen oft erst nach zwei Tagen. Letzte Woche hat meine Frage zur API-Freigabe von Montag bis Mittwoch gewartet, und unser Release ist von Donnerstag auf Freitag gerutscht. Ich will es in einem kurzen Call ansprechen.
reply: Jonas, darf ich dir kurz Feedback zu etwas geben? Letzte Woche hat meine Frage zur API-Freigabe von Montag bis Mittwoch auf eine Antwort gewartet, und dadurch ist unser Release von Donnerstag auf Freitag gerutscht. Wie siehst du das? ... Wäre es machbar, dass Fragen mit dem Label „blockiert“ innerhalb eines Arbeitstags eine kurze Antwort bekommen, auch wenn es nur „schaue ich mir Freitag an“ ist? Lass uns am Dienstag, 13. Oktober, kurz schauen, ob das klappt.
note: Unter Gleichrangigen: erst fragen, dann ein datiertes Beispiel mit seiner Folge, bei den drei Punkten wirklich zuhören, dann eine konkrete Bitte und ein Termin zum Nachfassen.

situation: I coordinate volunteers at our food bank. Gerald, a retired volunteer of six years who's brilliant at logistics, told a mum at the pickup table on Saturday to 'hurry up, other people are waiting', and she left without her box. He's unpaid and I don't want to lose him.
reply: Gerald, can I give you some feedback on the pickup table? On Saturday I heard you tell a mum to hurry up because others were waiting, and she left without her box. For a lot of people, coming here at all takes courage, so feeling rushed can be enough to keep them away. What's your read on Saturday? Going forward, when the line builds up, could you grab me to open a second table instead of speeding people along? Let's catch up after the shift on the 10th.
note: A volunteer gets the same shape as staff: private, one dated example, the real impact, and an ask that uses his strength with logistics.

situation: 我在运营组，同级的市场部同事阿伟最近三次在邮件里跟我有不同意见时，都直接抄送了我的领导和他的领导，其实当面五分钟就能说清。明天想约他喝咖啡聊一下。
reply: 阿伟，想跟你聊件事，可以吗？最近三次我们在邮件里有分歧，邮件都抄送了两边领导。结果小事变成了要领导表态的事，我们俩也都多花时间写解释。你那边是怎么考虑的？是不是之前有过说好的事没落实？以后有分歧，我们先打电话或者当面聊十分钟，定不下来再一起找领导，你看行吗？两周后我们再碰一下看看效果。
note: 对同级先问原因，抄送领导往往有背景，比如之前被放过鸽子；听完再提具体做法。

situation: I was promoted to lead our 5-person support team last month. Tom was my peer and is a good friend; we get drinks most Fridays. Twice this week he closed tickets as resolved without the customer confirming, and one customer reopened hers with an angry note. I need to raise it without it getting weird.
reply: Tom, can I give you some feedback on ticket closures? This is the part of the new role I find awkward with you, so I'd rather just say it straight. Twice this week you closed tickets as resolved before the customer confirmed, and one customer reopened hers with a pretty angry note. What's your read on those two? Going forward I need every ticket to wait for the customer's confirmation, or 48 hours with no reply, before it's closed. Let's look at how it's going in our one-to-one on the 13th.
note: Friend turned report: name the awkwardness once, then give him exactly the shape you'd give anyone else, and keep the friendship out of the ask.

situation: Rob, a senior engineer a level above me (not my manager), keeps repeating our new colleague Deepa's updates in standup in an exaggerated Indian accent, most recently on Monday and today. People laugh and Deepa laughs along, but she's barely spoken in the last two retros. I want to raise it with Rob privately.
reply: Rob, can I give you some feedback on something from standup? On Monday and again today, you repeated Deepa's update in an accent, and people laughed. I don't think you mean anything by it, but she's barely said a word in the last two retros, and I wonder if this is part of why. What's your read? I'd like the accent to stop; if something needs repeating, just repeat the point in your own voice.
note: Behaviour and impact, not a verdict on his character. If it carries on after this, take it to your manager or HR rather than having the same quiet chat again.

situation: 我28岁，刚当上销售组长。组员老刘45岁，干了十几年，客户关系特别好，但一直不用公司的客户系统，跟进记录都记在自己本子上。上周他请假三天，华信的客户来催报价，组里没人知道进度，客户投诉到了陈总那儿。明天想找他单独聊。
reply: 刘哥，有件事想跟您聊聊，方便吗？上周您请假那三天，华信来催报价，组里翻遍系统也找不到跟进记录，最后客户投诉到了陈总那儿。您的客户关系是组里最稳的，正因为这样，信息只记在本子上，您一不在就接不上。您平时不用系统，是觉得哪儿不顺手？以后每次跟进完，当天在系统里记三行就行：找了谁、说了什么、下一步。需要的话我陪您先把常联系的几个客户录进去，两周后我们再看看效果。
note: 年轻组长对资深组员：称呼尊重但不绕弯子，一件具体的事和后果，先问他的原因，要求小到当天就能做到。

situation: 我和同事小张是同组平级，工位挨着。他这两周经常在工位上外放短视频，声音不小。上周二下午我跟客户开电话会，客户问了一句“你那边在放什么”，挺尴尬的。想私下跟他说。
reply: 小张，有个小事想跟你说一下，方便吗？这两周你在工位上外放短视频，声音能传到我这边，上周二下午我跟客户开电话会，客户还专门问了一句“你那边在放什么”。我猜你可能没意识到声音传得这么远，你觉得呢？以后在工位看视频能不能戴上耳机？我下午有会的时候也会提前跟你说一声。
note: 平级同事的小习惯：说一个具体的时刻，问一句他的看法，提一个小请求，不用正式约谈。

situation: I manage Luis, an analyst whose dad died in July; he came back to work in August. Since then two reports for our client Halvorsen have come in late, due Sept 10 and Sept 24, and Halvorsen flagged the second one. I want to raise it kindly in our 1:1 on Thursday.
reply: Luis, can I raise something about work? The last two Halvorsen reports, due Sept 10 and Sept 24, both came in late, and they flagged the second one. I know these months since your dad died have been really hard, and I'm not expecting you to act as if they haven't been. What's your read on it, and what would help? Going forward I need the dates to hold, or to hear from you the day before if one's at risk, so I can move work around rather than find out from the client.
note: Name the loss once and plainly, then still make the ask; vague kindness leaves him guessing where he stands.

situation: 我是设计组组长。组里资深设计师雯雯能力很强，上周一晚上她没跟新人小杜打招呼，就把他做的首页方案整个重做了，周二客户评审直接讲了她的版本，小杜是在会上才知道的，事后跟我说挺受打击。明天和雯雯一对一，不想打击她的积极性。
reply: 雯雯，想跟你聊聊上周二评审的事，可以吗？上周一晚上你把小杜的首页方案整个重做了，周二评审直接讲了你的版本，他是在会上才知道的。我猜你是想让客户看到最好的方案，但结果是小杜这几天挺受打击，也没机会知道自己的方案差在哪儿。你当时是怎么考虑的？以后觉得谁的方案有问题，评审前一天先跟他和我说，让他自己改，或者你们俩一起讲。10月16日周五我们再看看效果。
note: 能力强的人越界时，问题不在她的水平，而在做法：说清具体那一次和对新人的影响，先听她的理由，再给一个能发挥她能力的做法。

situation: My report Nadia just did a run-through of our client pitch with me for Friday Oct 2. She read most of her slides word for word and took 25 minutes; we have a 15-minute slot, and pricing is the last section. I'm free Thursday at 2pm for another run-through. I want to say it now, in person.
reply: Nadia, can I give you some feedback on the run-through? You read most of the slides word for word, and it came in at 25 minutes against the 15 we have on Friday. If we run long, we lose the client before we reach pricing. What's your read on it? For Friday I'd like you to speak to the slides rather than read them and bring it in at 15, and I'd like one more run-through with you on Thursday at 2.
note: Feedback before the event, while it can still change the outcome, with the next check already booked.

situation: I'm head chef at a 40-cover bistro, and our kitchen uses red boards for raw meat. On Saturday night I saw our line cook Diego cut raw chicken and then the salad garnish on the same board without washing it; I pulled those plates before they went out. He's fast and the team likes him. I want to talk to him privately before Wednesday's shift.
reply: Diego, can I give you some feedback on Saturday? During service you cut raw chicken and then the salad garnish on the same board without washing it, and I pulled those plates before they went out. That's exactly how guests end up seriously ill. What was going on at that point in service? From now on, raw meat goes on the red boards only, every time, even when we're slammed. What would make that easier on your station? I'll check in with you after Friday's service.
note: Food safety is a health risk: one observation, the real impact, a firm rule and a check-in; his speed doesn't buy an exception.

situation: My report Hiro told me on Monday, the day our data migration was due, that it wasn't done because the vendor's API had been down since the Tuesday before. He's careful and conscientious, and I think he didn't want to bother me. I want to raise it in our 1:1 tomorrow.
reply: Hiro, can I give you some feedback on the migration? You told me on Monday, the day it was due, that it wasn't done, but the vendor's API had been down since the Tuesday before. If I'd known that week, I could have chased the vendor and warned the client, instead of explaining a missed date on the day. What made it hard to raise sooner? Going forward, I'd like a quick message within a day of anything blocking you, even if you think you can fix it yourself; an early heads-up will never annoy me. Let's check how that's working on Friday 9 October.
note: A careful person who sits on problems needs permission as much as a rule: say plainly that early bad news is welcome.

situation: Owen and I are both account leads. On Tuesday's video call with our client Brightwater he cut in three times before I'd finished, once in the middle of the pricing, and the client asked me to repeat the number. I want to raise it with him on a call tomorrow.
reply: Owen, can I give you some feedback on Tuesday's Brightwater call? Three times you came in before I'd finished, once in the middle of the pricing, and the client had to ask me to repeat the number. With two of us on a call, it makes us look less aligned than we are. What's your read on it? Next time, could you let me finish the point, and drop me a Slack message if you need to jump in? Let's compare notes after the next call.
note: Peer to peer, the impact is on the client, not on your pride; keep it there.

situation: 我是运营组长。组员小林昨晚在朋友圈吐槽“甲方又改到第八版了”，配图是带着客户新禾食品logo的设计稿截图，而客户的对接人跟他是微信好友。他平时做事很拼，改稿次数的事我也打算去跟客户谈。想今天找他单独聊。
reply: 小林，有件事想跟你聊一下，方便吗？昨晚你朋友圈那条吐槽改到第八版的，配图里有新禾食品的logo和设计稿，他们的对接人跟你是微信好友，很可能看得到。改八版确实磨人，你这阵子也特别拼，你自己怎么看这件事？我需要的是：那条先删掉，以后客户的稿子和信息不发朋友圈，憋屈了直接跟我说，改稿次数我去跟客户谈。周五我们再碰一下改稿流程。
note: 说清看到了什么、可能的影响，再给具体要求；先问他的看法，别直接定性为“不专业”。

situation: I manage Priya, a data engineer. In the last two weeks she's sent Slack messages at 1am or 2am at least six times, and on Tuesday her 2am deploy broke the morning dashboard. Two newer teammates have started replying late at night too. I want to raise it in our 1:1 on Monday.
reply: Priya, can I give you some feedback on late-night work? In the last two weeks I've seen messages from you at 1 or 2am at least six times, and Tuesday's 2am deploy broke the morning dashboard. I'm also seeing newer people start answering at night, and that's not a pace I want anyone to feel they have to match. What's going on for you at the moment? Going forward I'd like deploys to happen in working hours, and anything you write late to be scheduled to send in the morning. Let's look at how it's going in our 1:1 on Monday 19 October.
note: When the problem looks like dedication, name the impact on the work and the team, and ask about workload before the ask: it may be a capacity or burnout issue.

situation: 我是项目经理。组里来了三个月的小郑负责在客户微信群里回消息，这周我看到他两次回客户用的是“亲～收到哈哈哈”，客户问交付时间那次他回“应该快了吧”。昨天客户方的刘总私下问我交付时间到底定没定。想今天找小郑单独聊。
reply: 小郑，想跟你聊一下客户群回消息的事，方便吗？这周我看到你两次回客户用的是“亲～收到哈哈哈”，客户问交付时间那次回的是“应该快了吧”。昨天刘总私下来问我交付时间到底定没定，说明他心里没底了。你回的时候是怎么考虑的？以后群里回复语气正式一点，涉及时间的问题先跟我确认，再回一个具体日期。两周后我们再一起看看群里的情况。
note: 引用他的原话和客户的具体反应，不给他贴“不专业”的标签；先问他的考虑，再提要求，约好回头看。

situation: In our last four project planning meetings, my peer Martin, who chairs them, has asked a woman to take notes every time: me twice and Sofia twice, never any of the men. I don't think he's noticed the pattern. I want to raise it with him privately before next Tuesday's planning meeting.
reply: Martin, can I give you some feedback on the planning meetings? In the last four, note-taking has gone to a woman every time, me twice and Sofia twice, and never to any of the men. I don't think it's deliberate, but whoever takes notes is writing instead of contributing, and right now that's always the two of us. What's your read on it? Could we set up a rotation across the whole team, starting next Tuesday? Let's see how it's gone after a month.
note: Name the pattern with the count, not a verdict on him, and make the ask a fix he can run himself; if it continues, take it to your manager.

situation: I manage Zara, a marketing analyst. Her market-sizing memo for Thursday's leadership review cites '68% of mid-size firms plan to switch vendors in 2027' with no source; I searched and couldn't find it anywhere, and she's mentioned she drafted parts of the memo with an AI tool. The rest of the memo is solid. I want to raise it with her today and get a sourced version by Wednesday noon.
reply: Zara, can I give you some feedback on the market-sizing memo? It cites '68% of mid-size firms plan to switch vendors in 2027' with no source, and I couldn't find that figure anywhere. If someone at Thursday's review asks where it comes from and we can't say, it puts the whole memo in doubt, and the rest of it is solid. What's your read on where it came from? Going forward, every figure needs a source you've opened yourself, whatever tool helped with the draft. Can you send me the sourced version by Wednesday noon?
note: Keep it on the unsourced number and its impact, not on using the tool; the rule is the same for any draft.

situation: I'm a charge nurse on a surgical ward. On Monday and Wednesday this week my colleague Kelsey did handover to the night shift without mentioning patients' allergies, and on Wednesday the night nurse nearly gave penicillin to the patient in bed 4, who is allergic; she caught it at the last check. Kelsey has been here eight years and is great with patients, and I'm talking to her privately before her shift tomorrow.
reply: Kelsey, can I give you some feedback on handover? On Monday and Wednesday, allergies didn't come up in your handover to nights, and on Wednesday the patient in bed 4 nearly got penicillin, which he's allergic to. It was caught at the last check, but it was close. What's your read on it? From now on I need allergies said out loud for every patient at handover; would it help to make them the first line on the handover sheet? Let's check in on Friday 9 October.
note: Patient safety still gets private, specific feedback with one clear ask; near misses also go through your ward's incident reporting process.

situation: I manage Mateus, a support engineer in São Paulo; the rest of the team is in Berlin, five hours ahead, and he and I only overlap properly on Tuesdays. On the last two Monday handoffs, 21 and 28 September, his escalated tickets had no steps to reproduce, and each time the Berlin team lost about half a day waiting for him to come online to ask. I want to raise it today in a Slack DM rather than wait for Tuesday.
reply: Hi Mateus, can I give you some feedback on the Monday handoffs? On 21 and 28 September, the tickets you escalated didn't include steps to reproduce, and each time the Berlin team lost about half a day waiting for you to come online so they could ask. I'm writing now rather than waiting for Tuesday so it doesn't sit, but I'd genuinely like your read: is something making the steps hard to capture? Going forward, could every escalated ticket include repro steps, or a line on why they're missing? Let's talk it through live on Tuesday and look at the next two handoffs together on Tuesday 13 October.
note: Written feedback across time zones still asks for their side; keep it to one issue and book the live conversation in the same message.

situation: 同组的同事小雅下周三要做晋升述职，今天把PPT发给我，说“帮我狠狠挑毛病”。一共32页，前20页都在列她这一年做过的事，她最大的成绩是把客户续约率从78%提到91%，却放在第27页才出现。述职一共只有15分钟。我想在微信上回她。
reply: 看完了，最想提的一点是：续约率从78%提到91%是你今年最硬的成绩，现在放在第27页，15分钟里评委可能还没看到就到时间了。我建议把它挪到前三页，前面20页做过的事压缩成一两页，只留能支撑这个结果的。你自己觉得哪几页最舍不得删？改完想再过一遍的话，发我就行。
note: 对方主动要反馈也只挑一件最重要的事：看到了什么、有什么影响、具体怎么改，再问她的想法。

situation: My co-founder Leo and I run a two-person design studio. On client calls on 14 and 29 September he agreed to extra revision rounds for free, beyond the two rounds in our contracts, and the Harbor Dental job ran 11 hours over. I want to raise it with him over coffee tomorrow.
reply: Leo, can I give you some feedback on client calls? On the 14th and again on the 29th you agreed extra revision rounds for free, beyond the two in our contracts, and Harbor Dental ended up 11 hours over. That's time neither of us gets paid for. What's your read on it? Going forward, I'd like us to quote any extra round before saying yes, and I'm happy to draft a one-line answer we can both use on calls.
note: A co-founder is a peer with equal say: ask, then listen, then agree the rule together.

situation: チームリーダーをしています。メンバーの佐藤さんが、先週火曜と今週月曜の企画会議で、新人の出した案にすぐ「それは無理ですね、前にやって失敗したので」と返し、その後は誰も案を出さなくなりました。佐藤さんは経験豊富で頼りにしています。明日の1on1で伝えたいです。
reply: 佐藤さん、少しフィードバックをしてもいいですか。先週火曜と今週月曜の企画会議で、新人の案が出たとき、最初の一言が「それは無理ですね、前にやって失敗したので」でした。経験からの大事な指摘だと思っていますが、そのあと誰も案を出さなくなったのが気になっています。佐藤さんとしてはどう感じていましたか。これからは、懸念を伝えるときに「こうすればできるかも」を一つ添えてもらえると助かります。再来週の企画会議のあとに、また少し話しましょう。
note: 経験のある人の否定癖は、経験そのものを認めたうえで、会議への影響と具体的な言い方の工夫を一つだけ頼む。

situation: Our annual 360 reviews are due Friday, and I'm writing peer feedback for Ines, a product manager I work with every day. In the last three sprints she has changed priorities mid-sprint in Slack threads QA wasn't in, and twice our testers spent about two days on features that were then dropped. The form has a 'one thing to change' box, she'll see my name, and I'm happy to talk it through with her.
reply: One thing to change: in the last three sprints, priorities have changed mid-sprint in Slack threads that QA wasn't part of, and twice our testers spent about two days on features that were then dropped. That's testing time we couldn't get back before release. It would help a lot if mid-sprint changes were posted in the sprint channel with QA tagged, even as a one-line note. I'm happy to talk it through whenever suits you.
note: A written review can't pause for their side, so keep it to one dated behaviour, its impact and one ask, and offer the conversation; better still, mention it to her in person before the form lands.
